# Call recording consent

> Informational, not legal advice. Laws change and courts interpret them; confirm with a lawyer licensed in the jurisdiction before relying on any rule here.

Data: [`data/call-desk/recording-consent.json`](../data/call-desk/recording-consent.json). 64 jurisdictions, read as of 2026-10-11.

**Federal:** Federal law lets a party to a call record it, unless the recording is made to commit a crime or a tort. It is a floor: stricter state all-party laws still apply. ([18 U.S.C. 2511(2)(d)](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCODE-2023-title18/html/USCODE-2023-title18-partI-chap119-sec2511.htm))

**Across state lines:** When any party to the call is in an all-party state, follow that state's rule for the whole call. The practical standard is a spoken recording notice at the start of every recorded call, captured inside the recording, in every state. Kearney v. Salomon Smith Barney, Inc., 39 Cal.4th 95 (2006): California law applied to calls recorded in a one-party state with California clients, and a notice at the outset of the call complies.
